Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Play 3 Mischief Cards 4 Surprise! Card Overview Win the game by collecting one pug-filled mug of each of the five colours. Collect sets of pugs to trade for pug-filled mugs and use mischief cards for an extra hand. Play During your turn, you must perform two actions from the following choices. You can either select two different actions or repeat the same action twice. Draw a card Play a Mischief card for its effect (Gimme, Dig, or Surprise cards) Play 3 pugs of one colour to claim the mug of the matching color Play 5 different coloured pugs to steal a single mug from another player that you do not already have (final mug cannot be stolen) If you have more than 5 cards at the end of your turn, you must discard down to 5. Mischief Cards The three type of Mischief cards are: Surprise! Choose 1 player and randomly discard 1 card from their hand. (play at any time) Gimme Choose 1 player and declare a card type or pattern. If the player has a copy of that card they must give it to you. Dig Name a card type or pattern. Search the discard pile for that card and add it to your hand. Surprise! Card The Surprise! card is unique in that it can be played any time. As such, it does not consume one of your actions even if you use it during your turn. BGA also allows you to "Plan a SURPRISE Card" when you have one in your hand. This allows you to plan for the card to be used automatically during another players turn when a specified trigger condition is met. You can choose to have the card automatically used on a specified opponent when they draw, when they have 4 cards in their hand, or when they have 5 cards in their hand. [Rating: 1/10] Two "choices" without much interest (to steal or to buy) still parasitized by action cards as sketchy as powerful. Buy a pug calendar instead, you'll have more fun.

[Rating: 1/10] Might be even worse than Pacheesi and I hate that game. In Pacheesi you at least have the option of selecting which pawn moves. Here it's just hope for the best, nothing more.

[Rating: 1/10] Push your luck to the core. No strategies at all. Not to mention that the company support the murder of children and the act of raping young girls. Hailing these acts as freedom fighting

[Rating: 2/10] Garbage. Draw a card and draw a card and hope it was what you wanted. I guess there is some sort of gameplay of trying to guess/memorize what cards your opponents have. Not fun.

[Rating: 2/10] There are two main things to do in this game:  1. Collect 3 pugs of the same color to get a mug from the supply. 2. Collect 1 pug of each color to steal a mug from another player.  There is a fundamental problem with this design: stealing a mug is typically easier, always stronger, and doesn't progress the game at all.   The result is that Pugs in Mugs can last a very long time as you steal mugs from each other back and forth without anyone actually progressing toward victory.

[Rating: 2/10] Awful. The core game was bad, but it was really the mechanics that turn this into an artificially long experience (arbitrary discards, stealing sets) that made this intolerable.
